title: The five conditions of a lot that the older engine takes from its caller (a commercial overlay is present; a special purpose district is present; the whole lot lies within 100 ft of the corner point; the angle at which the two street lines meet; the lot lies in a special density area) come from the SAME evidence the decision step gathers, never from a typed-in value and never from the user as a fact; where the evidence is not known the engine is given a stand-in in the direction that withholds, no shown result ever rests on a stand-in, and the emitted document's scope lines say for each condition where it comes from (recorded, measured, the user's statement, or not known); the committed journey result and its saved drawings are regenerated through this path. It does NOT mount a route, does NOT touch the website's source, does NOT change the engine, the decision modules, the disclosure builder or any schema, and turns on NO switch. [the piece before the server route of work order Part A; owner rows R139, R229, R240, R241, R255, R256, R570, R582, R584, R588]
objective: THE ENGINE'S FIVE CONDITIONS COME FROM EVIDENCE (the piece before the server route of docs/plans/R6B_RESULTS_CONNECTION_WORK_ORDER_2026-10-06.md, Part A). THE FACTS TODAY (read at head 42d85651 by a research helper and in part by the orchestrator; VERIFY EACH in the source before you rely on it). (1) build_three_answer_inputs (services/api/app/contracts/evaluator_inputs.py, about line 429) REQUIRES from its caller five plain values: overlay_present, special_district_present, within_100_ft_of_street_line_intersection, street_line_intersection_angle_degrees, special_density_area. NO code under services/api/app calls it; the tests type the five values in (for example tests/scenario/three_answers/test_three_answers_three_way_emit.py, about lines 118 to 126, and tests/journey/test_215_16_northern_journey.py). (2) The engine reads them in inputs.py (height, coverage, rear-yard and dwelling-unit inputs, about lines 180 to 215): special district present makes every rule ask for review, so the engine gives no height, coverage, rear yard or unit figure; within 100 ft together with an angle of 135 degrees or less makes the rear yard 'not required'; special density area makes the dwelling-unit rule not applicable; overlay present adds a note only. (3) The decision step gather_result_ways (result_way_bridge.py, about line 307) reads its OWN evidence and never the five values: the recorded commercial overlay and special purpose district of the property profile (result_way_facts.py, about lines 276 to 281: present, absent or not read), the reach and the corner angle measured from the prepared outline and the site geometry (a measured figure or unknown), and the user's statement about the density area. (4) So today the two halves of one document can disagree. On the committed journey result the test typed 'within 100 ft: yes' and 'angle 90', and its scope block says 'The lot is assumed to lie within 100 feet of a street-line intersection' and 'No special purpose district is assumed to apply; this run does not read the special-district layer', while the same document withholds the coverage and the rear yard BECAUSE the measured lot reaches 103.93 ft and 144.60 ft, and while the program does read the recorded special-district columns. Measured by the research helper: with the typed special-district value flipped, all six shown heights disappear; so today's shown heights rest on a typed-in value. (5) The scope lines are built by build_scope_inputs (services/api/app/contracts/engine_disclosures.py, about lines 273 to 391) from the typed values, always with basis 'assumed' for four of the five; it cross-checks overlay_present against the recorded overlay fact and fails closed when they disagree (about line 222). The schema's scope_assumption (packages/contracts/schemas/v1/results.schema.json, about lines 568 to 593) needs key, value, unit, basis, statement; value is a string, a number or a boolean and CANNOT be null; basis is one of assumed, entered, fixture, city_records, survey_entered, approximate_tax_map, default: there is no 'not known' basis. THE READINGS (the orchestrator's; marked as readings for the reviewers to confirm or correct, continuing the numbering). (O33) ONE NEW ENTRY THAT TAKES EVIDENCE, NOT CONDITIONS. Add an entry beside run_engine_and_result_ways that takes what the server holds (the evaluator-inputs document, the study document, the option's housing program, the design choices, the property profile, the prepared outline, the site geometry, the user's optional statement about the density area, the result's id and time) and (a) gathers the decision step's facts FIRST, (b) derives the five conditions from those SAME facts, (c) builds the engine's inputs with build_three_answer_inputs, runs the engine, decides the ways and emits the document. The existing entry run_engine_and_result_ways keeps its behaviour for a caller that already holds engine inputs. Propose the SMALLEST shape that passes the import guards (tests/scenario/three_answers/test_result_ways.py: which files may name the decision module; tests/spatial/test_lot_reach.py: who may import the reach module) and makes no import cycle; justify it in five lines in the report. (O34) THE DERIVATION, in ONE new focused module services/api/app/scenario/three_answers/engine_conditions.py that takes PLAIN states (it does not import the decision modules, so the guard's list need not grow for it) and returns, for each of the five, the value for the engine AND where it comes from. Overlay: recorded present -> yes; recorded absent -> no; not read -> not known. Special purpose district: the same three. Within 100 ft and the angle: from the measured reach from the corner point and the measured angle; no outline or geometry -> not known; a lot that is not a corner lot -> not applicable. READING TO CONFIRM FROM THE RULE AND THE MODULE, not from this sentence: the engine's one yes/no means 'the whole lot lies within 100 ft of the point where the two street lines meet' (work order gap K4; the comparison text of REAR_YARD_WAIVER_WITHIN_100_FT in result_way_inputs.py). Density area: there is no evidence source today; the user's statement, when given, is used AS A STATEMENT; no statement -> not known. (O35) A STAND-IN ONLY IN THE DIRECTION THAT WITHHOLDS. The engine cannot take 'not known', and the engine is not changed here. Where a condition is not known the engine is given a stand-in chosen so that the engine itself gives no figure for what depends on it (special district: present; density area: inside one; within 100 ft: no). For each stand-in, PROVE the direction from the rule file, not from this sentence, and say so in the report (a stand-in in the wrong direction is the defect this task exists to remove). THE INVARIANT, tested over every input state: NO SHOWN RESULT (settled or conditional) OF THE EMITTED DOCUMENT RESTS ON A STAND-IN; wherever the decision step shows a result, every condition that result reads is recorded, measured or the user's statement, and equals what the decision step itself used. If you find a state where the decision step shows a result while a condition it reads is not known, STOP and report it: do not paper over it in the transform and do not change the decision module. (O36) THE SCOPE LINES TELL THE TRUTH. In the emitted document the scope line of each of the five conditions says where it comes from, in plain words: recorded (basis city_records, naming what is recorded); measured from the tax-map outline (the basis the geometry's own rank gives, with the measured figure); the user's statement (basis entered, saying it is a statement and not a recorded fact); not known (the line says it is not known and why, names the stand-in the calculation used and says that every result that depends on it is withheld; its value is the stand-in and its basis 'assumed', because the schema has no other way and the schema is read-only here; READING for the reviewers). No scope line of an emitted document may say that the program does not read something it reads, and none may contradict a reason given elsewhere in the same document. THE ORCHESTRATOR'S RULING ON WHERE: the lines are rewritten by the transform (three_way_document.py) from the per-condition sources the new entry hands it; engine_disclosures.py and evaluator_inputs.py stay byte-identical. When the transform is called without the sources (the older entry) the scope lines stay as the engine made them. STEPS. STEP 1: the table of input states and the red proofs (see the builder's brief). STEP 2: engine_conditions.py and its tests. STEP 3: the new entry and the scope lines. STEP 4: regenerate the committed journey result THROUGH THE NEW ENTRY (no typed-in condition), then its saved DXF and its site-plan drawing by the repository's own way; the massing drawing stays absent; read each regenerated file line by line and report every line that changed and why. Expected on the benchmark lot, from docs/reference-cases/R6B/cases/corner-reach.json row real-lot-reach and real-lot.json (never from the program's saved output): the overlay recorded (C2-2); no special purpose district recorded; the lot NOT wholly within 100 ft of the corner point (it reaches 144.60 ft); the street lines meeting at about 89.7 degrees; no statement about the density area. The shown values (the floor-area figures and the six heights, all conditional) and the set of withheld results must NOT change; what changes is the scope lines, and whatever the engine listed only because of the typed values (for example a rule version): name each such change. STEP 5: repoint the journey test and the wiring test to the new entry. STEP 6: if the review-register entry r6b-rear-yard-corner-waiver describes how the waiver's two inputs are obtained, bring it in line through register.json and the renderer (docs/zoning-rule-review/GUIDE.md); no human verdict. TESTS: one per input state with a table 'state, outcome, test id'; every expected value from the reference cases; a red proof on today's code for the contradiction of fact (4); one mutation proof per stand-in (flip its direction: a test must fail) and per derivation branch; a guard over every text the transform writes. NOT IN THIS TASK: any route, mount or switch; any website SOURCE file (only three website test files may change, and only if the regenerated result makes them fail); the engine (engine.py, inputs.py, answers.py, geometry.py, building_option.py, dwelling_units.py, rule_access.py, scope.py), the decision modules (result_way_*.py except the adapter), engine_disclosures.py, evaluator_inputs.py; any schema, schema copy or generated type; any rule-table value; the reason of the benchmark's rear yard (backlog row DB-198 stays owed); a NEW way of saying 'not known' in the contract (backlog row DB-196).
business_reason: The owner's rules: no fact about a lot is filled by a default or a guess; a fact that is not given withholds only what depends on it; what a user states supports only a conditional result; no value is applied without being shown; a withheld result shows no substitute (D-090 rows R229, R240, R255, R256, R570). The results document merged in wave 9 is honest about each result's way, but the older engine under it still takes five facts of the lot as typed-in values, and the document's scope lines repeat them as assumptions that contradict the document's own reasons. A server route cannot type them in and may not take them from the user as facts. This piece makes the five come from the evidence the program already gathers, so that the route (the next piece) and then the results screen (R582) can be built on a document that tells one story.
